fact_check_verdict: PASS: single primary peer-reviewed source (The Cryosphere 20, 6501-6519, DOI 10.5194/tc-20-6501-2026), full text read; no second outlet covers it, so every figure is attributed to the paper.

claims.spoken: Researchers at Washington University in St. Louis tracked when ice formed and melted on almost 31,000 lakes on Alaska's North Slope.
claims.verbatim_source: "We present the first comprehensive analysis of ice-on and ice-off timing across 30 774 lakes on the Alaska North Slope"

claims.spoken: The study covers five years, 2019 through 2023.
claims.verbatim_source: "for the period January 2019 through December 2023"
requires: five years is a baseline, never claim a trend

claims.spoken: The main tool is Sentinel-1, a European radar satellite that sees through cloud and the dark of polar night.
claims.verbatim_source: "The Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) operates independently of solar illumination and cloud cover"
requires: a sensor property, not a finding

claims.spoken: With passes on both orbits, the radar gets a fresh look at each lake about every four days.
claims.verbatim_source: "With both ascending and descending Sentinel-1 orbits providing a median observation gap of 4 d at this latitude"

claims.spoken: A machine learning model called a random forest reads the radar and labels each lake as ice or open water.
claims.verbatim_source: "We implemented the RF model using scikit-learn (Pedregosa et al., 2011) with 100 trees"
requires: it classifies past images, never say it predicts the future

claims.spoken: Most of the training labels came automatically from weather records, during long stretches of deep cold or real warmth.
claims.on_screen: ABOUT 62% OF LABELS · FROM WEATHER RECORDS
claims.verbatim_source: "Sustained temperature periods (10+ consecutive days below −20 °C or above +10 °C)"
requires: 10 or more days in a row below minus 20 C or above plus 10 C

claims.spoken: The rest of the labels came from clear-sky optical pictures from Sentinel-2.
claims.verbatim_source: "Sentinel-2 NDSI classifications provided the remaining labels during cloud-free conditions (30 % cloud threshold)"
requires: never say 30 percent of labels, the 30 is a cloud threshold

claims.spoken: It agreed with the optical satellite labels 94 percent of the time.
claims.verbatim_source: "The RF classifier achieved 94 % overall accuracy when evaluated against Sentinel-2 NDSI labels"
requires: say AGAINST SATELLITE LABELS, never against ground truth or field checked
never say ON HELD-OUT LAKES with the 94

claims.spoken: It was better at spotting ice than open water.
claims.on_screen: ICE CALLS STRONGER THAN WATER CALLS
claims.verbatim_source: "Performance was higher for the ice class (precision = 0.97 recall = 0.95)"

claims.spoken: Earlier radar-only studies usually landed around 80 to 85 percent.
claims.verbatim_source: "Previous single-sensor SAR studies typically achieved accuracies on the order of ∼ 80 %–85 %"

claims.spoken: On average the ice went out around June 8th.
claims.verbatim_source: "Across all lakes and years, mean ice-off occurred on day-of-year (DOY) 159 (8 June; standard deviation = 13 d)"

claims.spoken: And it came back around September 30th.
claims.verbatim_source: "Mean ice-on occurred on DOY 273 (30 September; standard deviation = 17 d)"

claims.spoken: That leaves about 114 days of open water a year.
claims.verbatim_source: "The resulting ice-free period averaged 114 d (standard deviation = 25 d)"

claims.spoken: Every degree farther north cut the open water season by about 23 days.
claims.on_screen: ABOUT 23 FEWER DAYS PER DEGREE NORTH
claims.verbatim_source: "with ice-free duration decreasing by 23 d per degree northward."
requires: a gradient across space, never a change over time

claims.spoken: Lake shape and size added only about two percent of explanation beyond temperature.
claims.verbatim_source: "morphometric parameters explained an additional 1.5 %–2 % of variance in ice phenology beyond temperature alone"

claims.spoken: Lakes that freeze to the bottom thawed about five days sooner, by median, than lakes with floating ice.
claims.on_screen: FROZEN TO THE BOTTOM · ABOUT 5 DAYS SOONER
claims.verbatim_source: "we see a modest five-day difference in median values between bedfast and floating ice for ice off"

claims.spoken: A simple temperature model matched the satellite ice-out dates for 82 percent of lakes, and freeze-up for 75 percent.
claims.on_screen: TEMPERATURE MODEL · ICE OUT 82% · ICE ON 75%
claims.verbatim_source: "82 % of lakes align with ADD estimates within twice the per-detection observation gap"
requires: say WITHIN A COUPLE OF RADAR LOOKS

claims.spoken: These lakes give off methane and carbon dioxide, and open water is when that gas trades with the air.
claims.verbatim_source: "These lakes emit substantial quantities of methane (CH4) and carbon dioxide (CO2) to the atmosphere"
requires: cited background, the study measured no emissions

claims.spoken: The paper says no field validation was done.
claims.on_screen: NO FIELD CHECK · PER THE PAPER
claims.verbatim_source: "no independent validation against field observations was performed."
requires: state as the paper's own limitation, never as a scandal

claims.spoken: Maybe tricky shorelines fooled the radar. The paper says lakes with big misses likely reflect complex shorelines hurting its detection.
claims.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: high residuals "likely reflective of complex shorelines negatively impacting our ice phenology detection"
requires: a possibility the paper raises, never a finding
pair with A FIELD CHECK WOULD SETTLE IT

claims.spoken: Instrumented lakes in earlier field work were open 80 to 110 days, short of this study's 114 day average.
claims.verbatim_source: "Arp et al. (2015) reported ice-free periods of 80–110 d for instrumented lakes"
requires: different lakes and years, never call it an error

cut.why: the paper says it was not

reserve.spoken: They picked 31,108 lakes big enough to see from space, and got ice dates for 30,774 of them.
reserve.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: lakes of 0.02 km2 or larger were selected (31 108), and phenology was retrieved for 30 774 (98.9%).

reserve.spoken: The lakes had to be at least two hectares, about five acres.
reserve.verbatim_source: "We selected all lakes ≥ 0.02 km2 (2 ha) to ensure each lake had a large enough number of pixels"
requires: small ponds are excluded, never say every lake

reserve.spoken: The study area runs from 69 to about 71 degrees north.
reserve.verbatim_source: "The selected study region (69-71.36° N, 163.85–141.02° W) contains 128 197 ALPOD lakes."

reserve.spoken: It uses six radar measurements, from inside each lake and from a hundred meter ring of land around it.
reserve.verbatim_source: "We trained the RF model on six Sentinel-1-derived features: VV and VH backscatter (dB) measured over the lake interior"
requires: the ring is 100 m of land around the lake

reserve.spoken: About 274,000 more looks, from 6,222 lakes the model never trained on, were kept back for testing.
reserve.verbatim_source: "An additional 274 079 observations from 6222 held-out (validation) lakes were reserved for testing."
requires: say ABOUT for the rounded figure

reserve.spoken: Counting every lake, the drop is closer to 30 days a degree, but outliers in the Brooks Range foothills push that up.
reserve.verbatim_source: "ice-free period decreasing by roughly 30 d per degree northward across all lakes"

reserve.spoken: The authors say the timing can help methane emission models and help plan targeted high-resolution observations.
reserve.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: the dates "provide critical timing constraints for methane emission models and for planning targeted high-resolution observation campaigns."
requires: never add roads, subsistence or aviation as named uses

reserve.spoken: The paper was published in The Cryosphere on November 12th.
reserve.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: article page lists Published 12 Nov 2026, received 27 Feb 2026, accepted 23 Oct 2026.
